title: Sensor Operator (SO), MQ-9 (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
3.     MOS 7314, Sensor Operator (SO), MQ-9 (MGySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. MQ-9 Reaper Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Sensor Operators
(SO) conduct multi-imagery sensor reconnaissance (MIR) and surveillance of
potential targets and areas of interest. The Sensor Operator detects,
analyzes and discriminates between valid and invalid targets using synthetic
aperture radar (SAR), electro-optical, low-light, and infrared full-motion
video imagery, and other active or passive acquisition and tracking systems.
Sensor Operators assist the pilot in air navigation, flight planning, and
other crew coordination tasks to achieve overall mission objectives. The
Sensor Operator utilizes laser target marking systems to provide target
identification and illumination, in support of other combat assets.



                                         3-455                       Enclosure (1)
 3148                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must have normal color vision.

            (3) Must have a five year term of enlistment.

            (4) Security requirement:

            (a) TS/SCI clearance paperwork must be initiated prior to arrival
at first course.

            (b) Must meet SCI eligibility guidelines based on a single scope
background T5 investigation.

            (c) Prior to conducting a lateral move, all applicants are
required to complete SCI pre-screen interview with HQMC SSO to determine TS/
SCI eligibility.

        (5) Must pass a class IV flight physical per reference (ai), Manual
of Naval Medical Department, Section IV, Article 15-100.

        (6) Must possess a GT score of 110 or higher.       This prerequisite is
non-waiver able.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the requirements for Basic Unmanned Qualification IV
(BUQ-IV) in accordance with CJCSI 3255.01 by completing the Basic Unmanned
Aircraft Systems (UAS) Qualification Course (M04VASD) at MCAS Cherry Point,
NC.

        (2) Complete the MQ-9A Sensor Operator Category I FRS Training Course
(M04H37D) at MCAS Cherry Point, NC, or the USAF MQ-9 Enlisted Course
(F34RPD1) Initial Qualification Training (IQT) School, Holloman AFB, NM.

        (3) A BUQ-IV individual will be awarded the PMOS 7314 after the
successful completion of MQ-9A IQT (F34RPD1, or M04H37D).

        (4) Upon award of PMOS 7314, Sensor Operators (SO) are authorized to
wear the Marine Unmanned Aircraft System Breast Insignia per MCO 1020.34.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to the MQ-
9 Sensor Operator Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Electro-Mechanical Technicians 17-3024.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

(b) Must meet SCI eligibility guidelines based on a single scope background T5 investigation. (c) Prior to conducting a lateral move, all applicants are required to complete SCI pre-screen interview with HQMC SSO to determine TS/ SCI eligibility. Requirements (1) Complete the requirements for Basic Unmanned Qualification IV (BUQ-IV) in accordance with CJCSI 3255.01 by completing the Basic Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Qualification Course (M04VASD) at MCAS Cherry Point, NC. matches: Accompany aircraft as a member of the flight crew to monitor and handle cargo in flight.

The enlisted flight crews in this OccFld assist in the planning and execution of tactical in-flight refueling and assault support missions, perform navigational duties, and operate and maintain the various communications and loading equipment in transport aircraft.
Operate airborne remote sensing equipment, such as survey cameras, sensors, or scanners.
MQ-9 Reaper Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Sensor Operators (SO) conduct multi-imagery sensor reconnaissance (MIR) and surveillance of potential targets and areas of interest.
Operate airborne remote sensing equipment, such as survey cameras, sensors, or scanners.

The Sensor Operator detects, analyzes and discriminates between valid and invalid targets using synthetic aperture radar (SAR), electro-optical, low-light, and infrared full-motion video imagery, and other active or passive acquisition and tracking systems.
Coordinate flight activities with ground crews and air traffic control and inform crew members of flight and test procedures.
Sensor Operators assist the pilot in air navigation, flight planning, and other crew coordination tasks to achieve overall mission objectives.
Install, calibrate, or maintain sensors, mechanical controls, GPS-based vehicle guidance systems, or computer settings.
For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to the MQ- 9 Sensor Operator Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
